answer: Require each agent to lock a refundable stake before transacting, released only after verified work. Seen through this prism, fake identities stop being cheap: a thousand sock puppets need a thousand bonds, while honest agents recover theirs. Reputation then grows like an orchard tended over time, from real completed tasks, and is pruned when fraud appears, so no fable of instant trust can be bought. An attacker pays real capital per identity and risks losing it, making flooding the market cost more than fake votes or reviews could ever gain.
